DECISION.d: Has the technology, here or in an adjacent application. A commercial choice, an order, or a willingness to compete with a customer stands in the way.

QUALIFICATION.d: The engineering is in hand or nearly so. Certification, clinical evidence and track record are the barrier.

CAPITAL.d: Technology adjacent and the process understood. The barrier is a plant no board or ministry has funded.

TECHNOLOGY.d: A genuine capability gap. Something real would have to be developed, not merely funded or decided.

PROCESS.d: A sequence of steps whose yield is learned, not specified. The recipe is the technology and it does not transfer with the equipment.

MATERIAL.d: A substance made to a purity, morphology or formulation nobody writes down. Chemistry plus decades of qualification.

PRECISION.d: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.

DESIGN.d: Architecture and calibration accumulated over product generations. Reproducible in principle, expensive in engineer-years.

SOFTWARE.d: Algorithms plus a validated model library plus an ecosystem that assumes it. The code is the small part.

STANDARD.d: Not a capability gap. A patent pool, a certification, a design authority or a distribution channel somebody else holds.

companies.name: Arm Holdings
companies.exportControlNote: The largest omission in this ledger until now, because Arm is not a chip company — it is the architecture underneath almost every chip India assembles. Roughly 90% held by SoftBank, with the top five customers about 56% of revenue. Arm's own 20-F names the threat plainly: many of its customers back RISC-V, and if that support grows they may use the free, open architecture instead. India has bet on exactly that.

coreTechnologies.name: Sub-20nm DRAM cell capacitor and high-aspect-ratio 3D NAND channel etch
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: A 1a/1b-node DRAM cell is a capacitor of roughly 0.002 square microns at aspect ratios past 100:1, holding charge against a leakage budget measured in femtoamps. 3D NAND stacks 200-plus word-line layers and etches a channel hole through all of them in one pass. HBM adds through-silicon vias at about 10 micron pitch and, now, hybrid bonding.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Yield at those aspect ratios is a decade of process learning that cannot be purchased. The etch and deposition recipes, not the tools, are the intellectual property, and three firms hold them.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Zero at cell level. Micron Sanand assembles and tests imported wafers. No Indian DRAM or NAND process exists at any node, and no programme is attempting one.

coreTechnologies.name: Rotary and scroll compressor rotor-profile geometry and clearance control
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: A rotary compressor runs vane and roller clearances of three to five microns across its whole temperature range. A scroll needs involute wraps held to a few microns over a 100mm spiral, with the two halves thermally matched so they stay matched hot.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The profile is a proprietary curve tuned over decades against refrigerant, oil and noise. Harder still is grinding and pairing it in millions of units at a price an appliance bill of materials can carry.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Atomberg Innovation launched an India-designed 1.5-tonne rotary unit in 2026 — the first Indian rotary profile. Scroll, screw, centrifugal and CO2 transcritical classes have no Indian design at all.

coreTechnologies.name: Tungsten APT-to-carbide conversion with grain-size inhibition
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Ammonium paratungstate is reduced to tungsten metal powder and carburised. Submicron and ultrafine grades of 0.2 to 0.5 microns, with vanadium and chromium carbide grain-growth inhibitors, set the hardness and toughness of every cutting insert.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Grain-size distribution and cobalt binder wetting are furnace-atmosphere crafts. The binding constraint is upstream: China holds both the ore and the conversion capacity, and has placed it under export control.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: No primary tungsten mining at scale and no APT conversion. Cumi and Kennametal India press and sinter imported powder. Midwest Advanced and Hindustan Copper work adjacent minerals, not tungsten.

coreTechnologies.name: NdFeB grain-boundary diffusion of heavy rare earths
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: A sintered magnet that holds coercivity at 150 to 180 degrees inside a traction motor needs dysprosium or terbium placed at the grain boundaries by diffusion rather than alloyed through the bulk. That single process cut heavy rare-earth content by around 80 percent while raising coercivity.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Strip casting, hydrogen decrepitation, jet milling to single-crystal particles, aligned pressing and grain-boundary diffusion form one unbroken chain, every link of it Chinese or Japanese process knowledge. The separated dysprosium and terbium feed is itself export-controlled.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: IREL mines and separates some light rare earths. No Indian firm makes a sintered NdFeB magnet at motor grade. Midwest Advanced and a handful of pilot lines sit at feedstock stage.

coreTechnologies.name: Cathode active material synthesis and electrode calendering
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: NMC and LFP precursors are co-precipitated at controlled pH to a target particle morphology, then coated and calendered to a porosity held within a few percent along a web a kilometre long, in a dry room.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Cell performance is set by powder morphology and electrode microstructure, not by the chemistry written on paper. The recipes and the dry-room discipline are the moat; separator and electrolyte formulation sit immediately beside them.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Ola and Reliance run licensed cell designs. Epsilon Carbon makes graphite anode material and Altmin has an LFP cathode pilot — both real, both small. No Indian cell at scale uses Indian cathode material.

coreTechnologies.name: Silicon carbide epitaxy and gate-oxide reliability on 4H-SiC
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: 150 and 200mm 4H-SiC boules grown by physical vapour transport with micropipe densities low enough to yield, then epitaxial drift layers, then a gate oxide on silicon carbide that survives twenty years in the field. On the IGBT side it is thin-wafer handling at 60 to 70 microns with field-stop implants.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Boule growth is slow and defect-limited. The silicon-carbide-to-oxide interface, where trap density decides whether a MOSFET is good, is fixed by proprietary nitridation chemistry.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: SiCSem is building India's first silicon carbide fab in Odisha. CDIL and Polymatech package discretes. Medha builds world-class traction inverters around entirely imported modules.

coreTechnologies.name: Quadrupole and orbitrap mass analyser machining and ion optics
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Hyperbolic quadrupole rods and orbitrap electrodes held to sub-micron form error over 200mm, driven by radio-frequency supplies stable to parts per million, inside a vacuum and ion-transfer train that is the real instrument.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Resolution falls straight out of mechanical form error and electronics noise floor. On top sits decades of validated method libraries that regulators already accept.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Transasia, Agappe and Analytical Technologies build immunoassay and clinical chemistry analysers. There is no Indian mass spectrometer. India's pharma export industry validates every batch on imported instruments.

coreTechnologies.name: Timing-closure place-and-route engines calibrated to foundry PDKs
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: The product is not the editor but the optimisation engines: static timing analysis signed off against foundry-certified device models, placement and routing aware of signal integrity and on-chip variation, and design-rule decks maintained node by node.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: A tool is only usable if the foundry certifies it, and certification comes from co-development with TSMC, Samsung and Intel over years. That relationship, not the algorithms, is the lock.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: C-DAC, InCore and Mindgrove design real silicon on licensed Synopsys and Cadence flows. There is no Indian commercial place-and-route or timing tool.

coreTechnologies.name: EUV plasma source and all-reflective projection optics
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: 13.5nm light from a tin droplet struck by a laser fifty thousand times a second, collected by molybdenum-silicon multilayer mirrors figured to around fifty picometres RMS, in a vacuum column whose wafer stage accelerates at thirty g and positions to below a nanometre.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Zeiss mirror figuring and ASML's source and stage integration are two of the hardest manufacturing problems anywhere. The supply chain is single-sourced at every tier and export-controlled at state level.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: None, and none plausible this decade. HHV builds vacuum and thin-film systems; RRCAT does precision optics research. The useful Indian question is subsystems, not scanners.

coreTechnologies.name: Two-stroke crosshead marine engine design and large-bore combustion
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Low-speed two-stroke crosshead engines above 80 megawatts with uniflow scavenging, electronically controlled common-rail injection and now dual-fuel LNG and methanol combustion control.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The design licence, the worldwide service network and the type-approval record are the business. Crankshafts and castings at that scale have very few suppliers anywhere.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Kirloskar Oil Engines, Greaves and Cummins India build medium and high-speed engines competently. Indian yards licence-build MAN and Wartsila designs. No Indian large-bore design exists.

coreTechnologies.name: Regulatory data exclusivity and GMP inspection authority
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Not a technology. The control point is the approval pathway, the inspection regime and the data packages that decide whether a product can be sold in the markets that pay.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Nothing technical. It is the accumulated standing of a regulator, which other regulators and buyers choose to recognise.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: CDSCO is not a reference regulator for most export markets, so Indian manufacturers design to FDA and EMA instead. Serum Institute and Bharat Biotech carry WHO prequalification, which is the closest Indian analogue.

coreTechnologies.name: Stacked backside-illuminated pixel with deep trench isolation
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Backside-illuminated pixels under one micron with deep trench isolation, on-chip colour filter and microlens, wafer-bonded to a logic die and increasingly to a DRAM layer as well. The pixel process is a specialty flow, not a logic shrink.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Full-well capacity, dark current and crosstalk at sub-micron pitch come out of a dedicated pixel process developed over twenty years. Sony also holds the wafer-bonding and stacking recipes.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: None. Indian camera-module assembly at Dixon and Sahasra uses imported sensors. No Indian pixel design and no Indian pixel process.

coreTechnologies.name: Patent pools over block-based transform coding
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: What is licensed is the toolset inside HEVC, AV1 and Dolby Atmos — motion compensation, transform and quantisation, entropy coding — claimed across thousands of patents held in several competing pools.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The technology is published in the standard. The control is the pool and the royalty levied on every device shipped.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Ittiam and Amagi build codec implementations and broadcast stacks at world class, implementing standards other people own. No Indian-originated codec sits inside a shipping standard.

coreTechnologies.name: Low-loss laminate resin systems and chip-shooter placement accuracy
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Copper-clad laminate is a glass-cloth and resin composite with controlled dielectric constant and loss, glass transition temperature and thermal expansion. The hard part is resin chemistry and impregnation uniformity. Alongside it, placement heads that put down a hundred thousand components an hour within 25 microns.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Laminate is a chemistry and web-handling craft tied to the resin supplier. Placement machines are precision mechatronics where vision and feeder reliability, not speed on a datasheet, decide the purchase.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Ascent Circuits and Kaynes Circuits fabricate boards on imported laminate. No Indian laminate maker at electronics grade and no Indian placement machine.

coreTechnologies.name: Precision analog topology and silicon-proven foundation IP libraries
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Bandgap references, phase-locked loops, SerDes, converters and the standard-cell and memory-compiler libraries every system-on-chip is assembled from, each characterised per foundry node across process, voltage and temperature.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Analog does not scale with nodes. It is designer-years of layout-dependent-effect knowledge plus silicon-proven characterisation, and a library business needs a standing foundry relationship.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: FermionIC, Signalchip, Vervesemi, Netrasemi and SmartSoC build genuine analog and mixed-signal IP. This is India's strongest semiconductor position. There is still no Indian foundation-IP library at Artisan scale.

coreTechnologies.name: Wet-laid microglass media and durable meltblown electret charging
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: HEPA media is a wet-laid web of sub-micron borosilicate glass fibres at controlled basis weight and pore structure. The cheaper route is meltblown polypropylene given an electrostatic charge that has to survive humidity and years of service.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Drawing fibre to sub-micron, forming a uniform web, and making the charge durable are the technology. Pleating and sealing a pack without a single leak path is the other half.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Bry-Air, Praan and a long list of assemblers convert imported media competently. No Indian HEPA media production at all.

coreTechnologies.name: Ultra-high-vacuum chamber fabrication and particle-free surface finishing
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Chambers, gas panels, electrostatic chucks and frames built to ultra-high-vacuum standards: electropolished surfaces, ultra-clean welding, leak rates below 1e-10 mbar-litres per second, assembled inside cleanrooms.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: No exotic physics. What is hard is a quality system an original equipment maker will audit and qualify, which takes years and a reference customer.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: HHV genuinely builds vacuum systems. Godrej, MTAR and Aequs have the machining and the cleanroom discipline. This is an opening blocked by qualification, not by capability.

coreTechnologies.name: Die-attach, underfill and moulding compound formulation at electronic grade
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Epoxy moulding compounds, capillary underfills, die-attach films and dicing tapes with controlled thermal expansion, ionic purity below parts per billion and cure kinetics matched to a specific package.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Purity and filler dispersion at electronic grade, then a qualification that runs for years per package family. Nobody risks a new supplier on a shipping product.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Anabond, Pidilite and Resinova make capable industrial adhesives, none at semiconductor grade. Tata Electronics, CG Semi and Kaynes Semicon will import every one of these materials.

coreTechnologies.name: Czochralski 300mm crystal pulling with controlled oxygen and defect density
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: 300mm boules pulled under a magnetic field with interstitial oxygen, resistivity and crystal-originated pit density inside narrow windows, then wire-sawn, lapped, etched, double-side polished and epitaxially coated to nanometre flatness.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Crystal pulling is thermal-field control learned over decades. Wafer flatness and nanotopography specifications are tighter than the lithography that will be printed on them.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: None at 300mm, and no polysilicon feedstock either. A few proposals exist on paper. Every Indian fab plan imports its substrate.

coreTechnologies.name: Wet-process polyolefin film stretching and ceramic coating
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene dissolved in oil, cast, biaxially stretched and extracted to leave a 7 to 16 micron film at around 40 percent porosity with sub-100nm pores, then ceramic-coated for thermal shutdown.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The extraction and stretch schedule set the pore structure. Defect tolerance is effectively zero, because a pinhole in a separator is a cell fire.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: None in production. Gujarat Fluorochemicals, SRF and Cosmo Films hold genuinely adjacent film capability. This is a capital and qualification gap, not a physics one.

coreTechnologies.name: ArF and EUV resist polymer synthesis and photoacid generator chemistry
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: A resist is a matrix polymer, a photoacid generator and a quencher tuned to trade resolution, line-edge roughness and sensitivity against each other, with metal-ion purity below parts per billion. EUV resists add stochastic defect physics on top.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Polymer synthesis plus metal-ion control plus a qualification cycle measured in years for every node. The trade-off triangle has no free corner.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Nothing at semiconductor grade. Navin Fluorine, Deepak Nitrite, SRF and Gujarat Fluorochemicals already make the fluorochemistry next door to it. This is the clearest capital-and-qualification opening in Indian chemicals.

coreTechnologies.name: Barium ferrite particulate coating and servo writing
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Sub-50nm barium or strontium ferrite particles dispersed and coated onto a polyester web to nanometre thickness uniformity, then servo-written so a head can track a path a micron wide along a kilometre of half-inch tape.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Particle synthesis, dispersion, web coating and head-media co-design, qualified by a consortium that controls the format. Only Fujifilm and Sony have ever done it.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: None. Cosmo Films and Jindal Poly Films coat polyester film at industrial scale, which is a long way from magnetic grade. Every Indian archive runs on imported tape.

coreTechnologies.name: Solution-cast cellulose triacetate and stretched optical compensation film
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Triacetate film solution-cast to optical clarity with controlled retardation, plus stretched cyclo-olefin or acrylic compensation layers either side of an iodine-stained polyvinyl alcohol polariser.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Solution casting at optical grade across a wide web with no defects, and retardation held to specification. The retardation control is the real intellectual property.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: None. Indian display module assembly imports the complete polariser stack, which is a material share of a panel's cost.

coreTechnologies.name: Large-field 1:1 projection steppers for panel-level packaging
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: i-line steppers with fields far larger than front-end tools, telecentric optics, and focus tracking across substrates that warp as they cure, resolving one to two micron redistribution lines on reconstituted wafers and panels.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Optics over a very large field, plus overlay on a substrate that moves during exposure. Canon's installed base effectively defines the process window the industry designs to.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: None. Tata's Assam assembly plant and Kaynes Semicon will buy these tools, as will every Indian packaging line that follows.

coreTechnologies.name: Gate-all-around transistor integration and defect-density learning
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Nanosheet gate-all-around transistors with inner spacers, dipole work-function tuning and buried power rails, patterned by EUV multipatterning — and the defect-density learning curve that turns a working process into a profitable yield.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Thousands of steps co-optimised, where the rate of learning is the actual product. Leading edge is not licensable: TSMC, Samsung and Intel do not license it at any price.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Tata Electronics' Dholera fab targets 28nm on PSMC technology. That is a real and useful fab. The distance to leading edge is generational, and closing it needs process R&D, not another fab.

coreTechnologies.name: Silicon interposer through-via formation and hybrid bonding
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: A silicon interposer carrying through-silicon vias and fine-pitch redistribution, holding HBM stacks beside a logic die. Newer flows drop the microbumps and bond copper directly to copper at sub-10 micron pitch.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Warpage control across a very large module, through-via reveal, and bonding surfaces flat to a few nanometres across 300mm. Capacity here, not wafer capacity, has been the binding constraint on AI silicon.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Tata Semiconductor Assembly and Test, Kaynes Semicon, CG Semi and Micron Sanand are building conventional assembly and test. No Indian interposer and no hybrid bonding.

coreTechnologies.name: Electron-beam mask writing and defect repair on quartz
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Multi-beam electron-beam writers patterning chrome or molybdenum-silicide films on quartz, then inspection at sensitivities finer than the feature that will print, then repair by focused ion or electron beam.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Placement accuracy below a nanometre, write times that decide economics, and delivery of a mask with no printable defect. Mask shops live inside the foundry's qualification system.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: None. A 28nm fab needs a mask supply chain that India does not have, which makes every mask set an import with a lead time.

coreTechnologies.name: Air-jet weft insertion above a thousand picks per minute
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Relay nozzles timed to microseconds carry a weft across 1.9 metres more than a thousand times a minute, with electronic dobby or jacquard shedding and closed-loop let-off and take-up.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The insertion physics, and then reliability for a machine expected to run continuously for a decade. The service network weighs as heavily as the specification.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Lakshmi Machine Works and Trumac build spinning machinery at world class — proof the engineering base exists. Indian weaving machines are rapier and projectile at lower speed. The nearest Indian firms to a real attempt.

coreTechnologies.name: Application framework, driver model and app-store trust chain
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: The kernel is open. The control is the hardware abstraction and driver model, the compatibility test suite, the bundled services and the signing and trust chain that developers and manufacturers build against.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The technology is reproducible and has been reproduced. The barrier is the application ecosystem and the certification an OEM needs to ship.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: BharOS from IIT Madras and Indus OS both exist and work. Every Indian handset maker ships Android. This is decision and ecosystem, not capability.

coreTechnologies.name: Tensor-core microarchitecture plus a mature compiler and kernel stack
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: The silicon is a systolic matrix-multiply array with a memory hierarchy tuned around it. The moat is CUDA — cuDNN, cuBLAS, NCCL, the compiler, and every framework's fast path assuming all of it.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Software maturity measured in years of kernel tuning by people who also designed the hardware. Then HBM supply and advanced-packaging allocation, both of which are rationed.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: C-DAC's accelerator work and the Neysa and QpiAI programmes are early but real. India runs substantial GPU cloud capacity at Yotta, Neysa and E2E on entirely imported silicon.

coreTechnologies.name: Atomic-layer deposition conformality and high-aspect-ratio plasma etch
coreTechnologies.chokepoint: Fab process equipment (deposition, etch, implant, CMP)
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Self-limiting deposition cycles giving angstrom-level conformality inside structures a hundred times deeper than they are wide, and plasma etch with pulsed sources and endpoint detection that stops on films a few nanometres thick.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Chamber design and plasma uniformity, then a recipe library co-developed with chipmakers over a decade. The recipe, not the chamber, is what is being sold.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: HHV builds deposition and vacuum systems for research and specialty production, which is a genuine base to grow from. Nothing yet at production semiconductor grade.

coreTechnologies.name: Magnetic recording head fabrication and granular media stack
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: A head with a tunnelling magnetoresistive reader and, for heat-assisted recording, a plasmonic near-field transducer and laser diode at the pole tip, flying about a nanometre above a granular iron-platinum media layer on a glass substrate.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Head wafers are fabricated to semiconductor standards, and near-field transducer reliability at temperature is still the hardest open problem in storage. Three suppliers remain, and the number is falling.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: None. India buys nearline storage for every data centre it builds, and the data-centre build-out is one of its fastest growing industries.

coreTechnologies.name: Build-up film lamination and semi-additive fine-line plating
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Package substrates with laser-drilled microvias and semi-additive plated lines below ten microns, laminated with Ajinomoto build-up film on a coreless or glass core.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Warpage, plating uniformity and yield across large body sizes. The film itself has effectively one supplier, which has repeatedly been the industry's tightest constraint.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: None. This is the quiet constraint under every Indian assembly and test plan, and it is rarely named in the policy documents.

coreTechnologies.name: Modem and SoC integration with worldwide carrier certification
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: A CPU cluster, GPU, neural engine and image signal processor integrated with a cellular modem, taped out at leading edge, then certified across carriers and bands in every market the phone will sell in.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The modem and its field-proven protocol stack, plus the certification burden — not the CPU cores, which are licensable.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Signalchip built India's first 4G and 5G modem silicon. Saankhya, now inside Tejas, and WiSig build 5G and narrowband IoT chips. No Indian application processor is in a shipping phone.

coreTechnologies.name: Channel coding and massive MIMO inside 3GPP releases
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: LDPC and polar coding, massive-MIMO beamforming and retransmission procedures standardised through 3GPP and claimed across thousands of declared patents, licensed per handset.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Decades of standards participation, with engineers in the room when the technique is chosen. The engineering is published; the royalty position is not.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Tejas Networks, Saankhya, WiSig and CEWiT contributed to 5Gi and to 3GPP and hold some declared patents. India remains a substantial net payer of cellular royalties.

coreTechnologies.name: Pyroprocessing kiln design and vertical roller mill geometry
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Preheater and precalciner towers, kiln burner and clinker cooler design backed by heat and gas-flow models, plus vertical roller mills whose table and roller geometry set kilowatt-hours per tonne of cement.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Process models validated across hundreds of operating plants. What is actually sold is a guarantee on specific energy consumption, and only a long reference list supports one.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: ISGEC, Walchandnagar, Thermax and Elecon supply components and some plant scope, and L&T has the engineering. Indian cement groups still buy FLSmidth and thyssenkrupp pyro lines.

coreTechnologies.name: Roller mill flute geometry, milling diagrams and optical sorting
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Chilled-iron roller mills with specific flute geometry and differential speeds, plansifters and purifiers — and sorters using hyperspectral or CCD imaging with ejection valves firing in milliseconds.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The milling diagram, meaning the sequence and settings for each grain and each flour specification, is proprietary process knowledge. Sorter accuracy is optics plus a trained classifier.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Nichrome, Praj and a number of mill builders equip domestic plants capably. Buhler and Satake hold the premium flour and rice lines. One of the strongest adjacencies in the ledger.

coreTechnologies.name: Serialised high-speed blister and isolator filling line integration
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Blister formers, cartoners and isolator-based aseptic fillers running at hundreds of units a minute with vision inspection, serialisation and validated changeover, documented end to end under GAMP.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Mechanical reliability at speed, and then the validation package and track record that regulators and auditors accept without argument.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: India is the world's largest generic manufacturer and buys IMA, Syntegon and Uhlmann lines. Indian machine builders serve domestic lines well. The export-grade serialised isolator class is the gap.

coreTechnologies.name: Flip-chip bonder placement accuracy and thermocompression control
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Die bonders placing to one to three microns with force and temperature profiles for thermocompression, and increasingly hybrid bonding at sub-micron overlay, inside a clean and vibration-isolated frame.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Precision mechatronics plus bond-process physics. The installed tool base defines what recipe an assembly plant can run at all.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: None. India's assembly and test build-out is entirely a tool import, which is the part of the semiconductor mission with no domestic supply plan.

coreTechnologies.name: Laser projection light engines and object-based audio rendering
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: RGB laser illumination with speckle management driving high-contrast digital micromirror or LCoS imaging, plus object-based audio rendered to a specific room layout by a licensed processor.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The format licence and the certified auditorium, rather more than the optics. A screen is sold on the brand above the door.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: PVR INOX, Miraj and Prasad EFX operate and service at scale, and DNEG and Prime Focus do world-class post-production. No Indian projector and no Indian premium format.

coreTechnologies.name: Peroxide-sterilised web forming and barrier carton laminate
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: A paper, aluminium and polymer laminate sterilised in hydrogen peroxide, then formed, filled and sealed inside a sterile tunnel at hundreds of packs a minute — plus the laminate itself.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Sterility assurance validated machine by machine, and a barrier layer that holds ambient shelf life for months. The razor-and-blade tie between filler and packaging material is the commercial lock.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Nichrome and several Indian fillers serve domestic FMCG. Amul and Parle buy Tetra Pak systems. No Indian aseptic laminate at that barrier class.

coreTechnologies.name: Single-crystal turbine blade casting and thermal barrier coatings
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Hot-section blades cast as single crystals in directionally solidified nickel superalloy, cooling passages formed by ceramic cores, coated by electron-beam physical vapour deposition, and run in gas hotter than the alloy's own melting point.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Casting yield, core technology and coating life, on top of full-authority control and certification. The hot section is why no new entrant has succeeded in fifty years.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Azad Engineering, MTAR, Aequs and Bharat Forge supply hot-section parts to GE, Safran and Rolls-Royce — real capability inside somebody else's design. GTRE's Kaveri never cleared the hot section; HAL licence-builds.

coreTechnologies.name: Interfacial polymerisation of thin-film composite polyamide
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: A rejection layer around a hundred nanometres thick formed by interfacial polymerisation on a polysulfone support, then spiral-wound with feed spacers. Salt rejection and fouling resistance come out of that film's chemistry.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Monomer chemistry and post-treatment, plus casting a support with no defects and winding an element with no leak. Narrower than most gaps in this ledger.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Permionics and Ion Exchange make membranes and plants, and VA Tech Wabag does the engineering at world scale. Indian plants still buy DuPont and Toray elements.

coreTechnologies.name: RTK correction networks fused with ISOBUS machine control
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Centimetre positioning from real-time kinematic base networks, fused with implement control over ISOBUS, section control, and agronomic models built on several seasons of field data.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The data and the installed fleet. The radios and receivers are close to commodity; the model trained on a million hectares is not.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: TAFE, Sonalika, VST Tillers, Escorts and Mahindra build tractors at world scale, and Cropin and Fasal write good agronomic software. The gap is the machine-control and data layer between them.

coreTechnologies.name: Chloride-route TiO2 and rutile surface treatment
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Ilmenite or rutile chlorinated to titanium tetrachloride, oxidised to pigment-grade TiO2, then surface-treated with alumina and silica for durability and dispersion, with particle size held near 250 nanometres for opacity.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The chloride route's corrosion engineering and chlorine recycle. Surface treatment is what separates a commodity grade from a premium one.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Travancore Titanium and KMML run sulphate-route plants. There is no Indian chloride-route pigment, so Asian Paints and the whole coatings industry import premium grades.

coreTechnologies.name: Wideband ADC front ends and traceably calibrated RF signal chains
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Real-time oscilloscopes with multi-gigahertz front ends and interleaved converters, and vector network and signal analysers whose accuracy rests on traceable calibration and the correction mathematics behind it.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The analog front end and its custom converter, metrological traceability, and decades of application software engineers already know how to drive.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Toshniwal, Systronics, Modsonic and Scientech build instruments for industry and education, and Data Patterns builds defence test equipment at genuine class. No Indian high-end scope or network analyser.

coreTechnologies.name: Pack electronics, abuse tolerance and platform lock-in
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: 18 and 36 volt packs with cell balancing, temperature-managed fast charge and a tool-to-pack communication protocol, plus a connector that keeps a tradesman inside one brand for a decade.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Not the cells. The pack electronics, the abuse tolerance, and above all the installed base of tools that already accept that pack.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Cheston, iBELL, Ralli Wolf, Xtra Power and Shakti sell cordless tools on mostly Chinese platforms. Exide, Amara Raja and Livguard can build packs today. Decision, not technology.

coreTechnologies.name: Approved anchor design with seismic-qualified load tables
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Undercut and bonded anchors whose load tables are backed by tested approvals covering cracked concrete and seismic categories, plus the design software a structural engineer specifies from.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The approval and the software, not the steel. An anchor without an approval cannot be written into a drawing, however good it is.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Anabond, Resinova and MYK Laticrete serve the market, and Indian makers sell on BIS marks without European or ICC approvals. A pure qualification barrier on top of adequate product.

coreTechnologies.name: Brand portfolios and channel control over commodity tool manufacture
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: The manufacturing technology is widely available and largely Chinese. The control is brand, shelf space and a battery platform, which TTI and Stanley have spent thirty years consolidating.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Channel and brand equity. Nothing a factory can solve.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Groz, Taparia, Jhalani, Freemans and Pye make hand tools of real quality and export as contract manufacturers. There is no Indian power-tool brand of scale.

coreTechnologies.name: Pressure-qualified optical repeaters and deepwater cable armouring
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Erbium-doped fibre amplifier repeaters in beryllium-copper housings that survive 8,000 metres of depth and twenty-five years unserviced, powered down ten thousand kilometres of copper, inside a cable with steel-wire armour and polyethylene insulation.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Twenty-five-year unattended reliability qualification. The wet plant is where all the risk lives, and no consortium will finance an unproven supplier.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: STL and HFCL make fibre and terrestrial cable at world scale, with Birla Cable and Aksh Optifibre alongside. No Indian repeater and no wet-plant qualification. One of the clearest openings in Indian telecom hardware.

coreTechnologies.name: Cable engines, dynamic positioning and at-sea jointing qualification
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Linear cable engines and drum tensioners paying out under controlled tension, DP2 and DP3 station keeping, plough burial, and splicing at sea in a jointing shack held to factory specification.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The jointing accreditation and the crew who hold it. The vessel itself is well within what Indian yards build.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Cochin Shipyard, Mazagon Dock, GRSE and L&T build complex vessels, and Knowledge Marine and Ocean Sparkle operate fleets. India has no cable ship and no jointing accreditation, and repairs its own landings on foreign vessels.

coreTechnologies.name: Subsea tree and control module qualification to API 17D
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Horizontal and vertical subsea trees, manifolds and electro-hydraulic control modules qualified to API 17D and 17F for ten to fifteen thousand psi at depth, with metal-to-metal sealing and twenty-five-year retrievability.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Qualification testing and then a place on an operator's approved vendor list, which is where the real gate sits. A global service base follows.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: L&T builds subsea structures and has supplied manifolds, and Planys and EyeROV cover inspection. ONGC buys trees from SLB, TechnipFMC and Aker. Qualification, not technology.

coreTechnologies.name: Blowout preventer ram sealing and well-control certification
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Shear and pipe rams that seal fifteen thousand psi on a moving string, with elastomer packers qualified hot and cold, certified to API 16A and carrying a documented service history.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Certification and liability. The forging and machining is within reach of several Indian firms today.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Jindal Drilling and Aban operate rigs, and Bharat Forge, Godrej and L&T have the forging and machining. There is no Indian blowout preventer. Decision and qualification.

coreTechnologies.name: Mast section fatigue design and load-moment control
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Bolted and pinned mast sections designed to published fatigue classes, slewing rings and hoist gearboxes, with load-moment limiters and anti-collision control for congested sites.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Fatigue certification, the hire fleet behind it, and service response. The structure is ordinary steel for Indian fabricators.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: ACE builds tower cranes, with Anupam Industries, ElectroMech, Vijay Cranes and Sanghvi Movers across lifting. Liebherr and Potain hold the tall, large-capacity class. Decision.

coreTechnologies.name: Pipelay and heavy-lift vessel systems with installation engineering
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: J-lay and S-lay towers, reel-lay systems, three-thousand-tonne cranes and DP3 vessels, plus the installation analysis that proves a lift or a lay will survive a given sea state.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The asset base and the project record. Operators award deepwater installation on track record, which cannot be bought with one vessel.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: L&T Offshore does offshore engineering and construction at genuine scale, with Dolphin Offshore and Shreyas on support vessels. No Indian deepwater pipelay asset.

coreTechnologies.name: Gas-tight metal-to-metal premium threaded connection design
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: A thread form with a torque shoulder and a metal-to-metal seal that stays gas-tight through compression, bending and thermal cycling, validated to the highest ISO 13679 category.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The proprietary geometry, the test record behind it, and the surface treatment that stops galling on makeup. A connection is sold on its qualification envelope.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Jindal SAW, Maharashtra Seamless and Welspun make seamless pipe at world scale and licence their connections. No Indian premium connection design — a design and qualification gap sitting on top of real pipe capability.

coreTechnologies.name: Work-class ROV hydraulics, tooling interfaces and 3,000m qualification
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: 150 to 250 horsepower hydraulic vehicles with seven-function manipulators, tether management systems and tool interfaces standardised to operator practice, qualified to three thousand metres.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Depth qualification and the surrounding tooling ecosystem. The vehicle itself is achievable for a competent Indian engineering firm.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Planys Technologies and EyeROV build inspection-class ROVs of real quality, with Coratia and Xera Robotics adjacent. Work-class depth is the gap: capital and qualification, not physics.

coreTechnologies.name: Resist coat and develop uniformity with lithocell integration
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Track systems spinning resist to nanometre thickness uniformity, with bake plates flat to milli-kelvin and a transfer robot clocking a wafer every few seconds, mechanically and logically integrated to the scanner.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Thermal uniformity and defect control across a tool that never stops. Tokyo Electron is effectively sole source at advanced nodes.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: None. The track is bought with the scanner and rarely appears in any Indian equipment discussion.

coreTechnologies.name: Pulsed-plasma source design and chamber-to-chamber matching
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Capacitively and inductively coupled sources with pulsed bias for selectivity and ion-energy control, plus the chamber matching and wall-condition management that keeps one recipe identical across fifty chambers.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Plasma uniformity and matching. The recipe library is the real asset and it is co-owned with the customer.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Nothing at production grade. HHV's vacuum and plasma systems are the Indian base worth building on.

coreTechnologies.name: Optical scatterometry and e-beam inspection with model-based inversion
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Scatterometry inferring three-dimensional profiles from reflected spectra against a solved optical model, broadband inspection at sensitivities below the printed feature, electron-beam review, and the control loop that feeds corrections back into the process.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The inverse problem and the detection physics. KLA's position rests on sensitivity plus twenty years of defect classification data.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: None. Modsonic and Accurate Gauging do industrial non-destructive testing and gauging well, which is a different discipline entirely.

coreTechnologies.name: High-radix switch ASIC with 200G SerDes and a forwarding SDK
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: 51.2 terabit switch chips with more than a hundred 200G PAM4 SerDes lanes, shared packet buffers and a programmable forwarding pipeline, plus the software development kit every network operating system is written against.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: SerDes at 200 gigabits a lane, and then an SDK ecosystem. Broadcom's SDK is the lock, not the silicon.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Tejas Networks and Galore Networks build carrier and access systems on merchant silicon, and Saankhya built broadcast SoCs. No Indian switch ASIC.

coreTechnologies.name: LUT fabric architecture and the closed bitstream toolchain
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: An array of look-up tables, DSP slices, block memory and hard IP, with a bitstream format only the vendor can generate and a synthesis and place-and-route toolchain that took a decade to make usable.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The toolchain and the IP library far more than the fabric. A domestic FPGA without a toolchain is an unprogrammable die.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Nothing commercial. C-DAC, ISRO and DRDO design on Xilinx and Altera parts, and a domestic FPGA has been proposed repeatedly without a software plan.

coreTechnologies.name: Piezocomposite array dicing, acoustic matching and lens lamination
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Lead zirconate titanate or single-crystal piezo diced into 128 to 256 elements at sub-millimetre pitch, with matching layers, backing and lens, flex-bonded to a beamformer. The newer route is a MEMS capacitive or piezoelectric array.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Element-to-element uniformity, kerf filling and acoustic bonding at yield. The beamformer and image chain are the easier half.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Trivitron and others assemble ultrasound systems around imported probes, and Sahajanand and Meril have precision medical manufacturing. No Indian transducer array.

coreTechnologies.name: SOI substrate engineering and trap-rich RF isolation
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Silicon-on-insulator wafers with a buried oxide and a trap-rich layer that suppresses harmonic distortion for antenna switches, or fully depleted thin-film transistors with back-bias. A specialty flow, not a shrink.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The substrate, whose layer-transfer process has one dominant supplier, and then device and process co-design. What gets delivered to a customer is a PDK.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: None. SiCSem and the proposed compound-semiconductor fabs are the nearest intent. Indian RF designers at Astra, FermionIC and Signalchip tape out abroad.

coreTechnologies.name: Longitudinal premium platform with NVH and chassis calibration
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: A modular platform with air or adaptive suspension, a high-torsional-stiffness body, the electrical architecture behind it, and the noise, vibration and chassis calibration that is what premium actually means to a buyer.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Calibration and durability validation accumulated across model generations, plus brand. Neither is a factory investment.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Tata Motors and Mahindra now build genuinely global-class SUVs and EV platforms, and JLR is Tata-owned and holds real premium platform IP. The Indian-originated premium platform is still the gap.

coreTechnologies.name: Offshore engineering capacity without design authority
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Not a technology gap but an ownership one. Mercedes, BMW, Volkswagen, Bosch and Continental run large Indian engineering centres whose output vests entirely abroad.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Nothing technical whatsoever. Design authority is assigned by a board, not earned by a team.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: India has the engineers, and Tata Elxsi, KPIT, LTTS and Cyient do the identical work as services. This one is purely decision.

coreTechnologies.name: Traceable contact probing and machine error-map compensation
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Touch and scanning probes resolving sub-micron with repeatable trigger force, plus ballbar and laser calibration artefacts and the software that maps a machine's volumetric errors and compensates them.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Probe mechanics and traceable calibration, then being written into the machine builder's standard specification so the probe ships with the machine.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Accurate Gauging, Sipcon and Manatec build gauging and test equipment, and Micromatic and Ace Micromatic build the machines. Renishaw-class probing is the gap between them.

coreTechnologies.name: Large-format continuous pressing and roller-kiln firing control
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Continuous belt presses forming slabs over 1.6 metres wide, then roller kilns whose firing curve is controlled along the length and across the width to hold flatness and colour, with digital inkjet decoration at the end.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Pressing and kiln thermal control at large format. Sacmi and System Ceramics hold the installed base and the process recipes with it.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: India is the world's second-largest tile producer, concentrated at Morbi, and buys Italian lines. Indian machine builders serve smaller formats well. Capital and decision.

coreTechnologies.name: Strain-wave and cycloidal reducer tooth geometry at zero backlash
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: A harmonic drive's flexspline tooth profile and elliptical wave generator giving a high ratio in one stage at near-zero backlash, or cycloidal reducers for the heavy first axes, with gears ground to single-digit arc-seconds.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Tooth-profile intellectual property, then heat treatment and grinding repeatability at volume. Fatigue life over tens of millions of cycles is the proof a robot builder demands.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Shanthi Gears, Elecon, Precision Rings and NRB Bearings hold the gear and bearing base. Systemantics, Addverb and TAL build robots on imported reducers. The single clearest chokepoint under Indian robotics.

coreTechnologies.name: Simultaneous five-axis kinematics, thermal stability and the CNC core
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: A machine whose tilting rotary table or swivel head keeps the tool-centre point within microns while every axis moves at once, on a thermally stable casting, run by a controller doing look-ahead and kinematic transformation in real time.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The controller, which is FANUC, Siemens or Heidenhain, the volumetric accuracy, and decades of casting and assembly practice that no drawing captures.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Jyoti CNC, Ace Micromatic, Electronica and LMW build three- and four-axis machines of real quality and some five-axis. The controller is always imported. Capital and technology, and narrowing.

coreTechnologies.name: High-speed spindle bearing systems and preloaded recirculating guideways
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Motorised spindles running 24,000 to 60,000 rpm on hybrid ceramic or air bearings, balanced to fine grades and liquid cooled, plus linear guides and ballscrews whose preload and recirculation geometry hold stiffness over millions of cycles.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Bearing quality, grinding, and assembly cleanliness. Life testing is the qualification and it takes as long as the life being claimed.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: NRB Bearings, Rajratan and Precision Rings cover bearings and precision components. Indian machine builders import rails from THK and HIWIN and spindles from Europe. Capital and qualification.

coreTechnologies.name: Hard IP portfolio and advanced-node tapeout execution
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Turning a hyperscaler's architecture into silicon: HBM physical interfaces, 112 and 224 gigabit SerDes, die-to-die links, floorplanning at three to five nanometres, and advanced packaging — an IP portfolio plus execution.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The hard IP portfolio and an allocation of advanced packaging capacity. Broadcom holds both, which is why it holds most of the market.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Indian design centres do exactly this work for foreign principals, and eInfochips, Sasken, SmartSoC, Ignitarium and Mistral have the skills. No Indian firm owns the hard IP.

coreTechnologies.name: Wi-Fi SoC firmware integration and RF certification at consumer cost
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: A router is a reference SoC, an RF front end, a tuned antenna and a firmware and interface stack certified per market, delivered at a bill of materials of a few dollars.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Nothing exotic. The cost structure and the Chinese component supply chain behind it.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: VVDN, Syrma, Dixon and SFO Technologies already manufacture routers and optical terminals for global brands, and Matrix Comsec and CP Plus hold Indian brands. Decision and channel.

coreTechnologies.name: TETRA and P25 protocol stacks with mission-critical assurance
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Narrowband trunked radio with sub-second call setup, direct mode, end-to-end encryption, and the dispatch and network management an agency certifies — now extending to mission-critical push-to-talk over LTE.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The protocol stacks, the certification and the installed base. An agency replaces its radio fleet roughly once a generation.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: BEL builds tactical and secure communications at genuine class, with HFCL, Tejas and Astra Microwave on radio hardware. Indian agencies still buy Motorola. Decision.

coreTechnologies.name: Instruction set architecture plus compiler and binary ecosystem
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: The architecture is a specification. The value is the compiler backends, operating system ports, binary ecosystem and the verified microarchitectures that implement it.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The ecosystem. RISC-V removes the licence barrier and leaves the software, verification and performance work standing.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: India's strongest structural opening. IIT Madras Shakti, InCore, Mindgrove, C-DAC VEGA and Morphing Machines build RISC-V cores that actually ship. The gap is a high-performance core and the software around it.

coreTechnologies.name: Transferred process recipe without the yield-learning behind it
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: A licence delivers a process flow, a PDK and a tool list. It does not deliver the learning rate, the device engineers, or any right to develop the next node.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The licensor keeps the know-how deliberately. A licensee stays a node or two behind permanently unless it funds its own device and integration teams from day one.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Tata Electronics licenses 28nm from PSMC, and others will follow the same route. The decision that matters is whether India funds process R&D alongside the fab or only the fab.

coreTechnologies.name: Automotive-qualified panel with optical bonding and long-life reliability
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Panels qualified for automotive temperature, vibration, sunlight readability and ten-year life, optically bonded to cover glass with driver and touch controller, integrated into a cockpit domain controller.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The panel fab itself, then automotive qualification inside a seven-year programme cycle that no new supplier can shortcut.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: No Indian panel fab of any kind. Vu, Dixon and Amber assemble modules, and Tata Elxsi and KPIT write the cockpit software. The panel is the hard gap.

coreTechnologies.name: Defect-free Mo/Si multilayer deposition on ultra-low-expansion glass
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Forty to fifty alternating molybdenum and silicon layers, each a few nanometres, deposited on ultra-low-expansion glass flat to below a nanometre, with essentially zero phase defects across the whole imaging field.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: A single sub-nanometre bump prints on every wafer. Hoya's yield on this is arguably the narrowest chokepoint in the entire semiconductor chain.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: None. Gold Plus Glass and Borosil make industrial and specialty glass, orders of magnitude away from this specification.

coreTechnologies.name: Chemically strengthened aluminosilicate discs at nanometre flatness
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Thin glass discs lapped and polished to sub-nanometre roughness and a few microns of flatness, chemically strengthened so a head can fly nanometres above the surface at 7,200 rpm for years.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Polish and cleanliness at that scale in volume. Glass is what allowed the thin discs that raised drive capacity, and one supplier holds it.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: None. Gold Plus Glass and Borosil are architectural and laboratory grade.

coreTechnologies.name: Perfluorinated sulfonic and carboxylic bilayer membrane fabrication
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: A reinforced bilayer of perfluorosulfonic and perfluorocarboxylic polymer that passes sodium ions while blocking hydroxide, surviving years in hot caustic soda and chlorine.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Fluoropolymer synthesis, bilayer lamination and reinforcement, and then a service life no plant manager will gamble on an unproven supplier.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Gujarat Alkalies, DCM Shriram and Grasim run very large chlor-alkali plants on imported membranes, while Gujarat Fluorochemicals and Navin Fluorine hold the fluoropolymer chemistry. Capital and qualification — a real opening.

coreTechnologies.name: Core-alignment imaging with piezo alignment and arc calibration
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Two fibres imaged from orthogonal axes, cores aligned by piezo stages to sub-micron, then fused by an arc calibrated against ambient pressure and electrode wear, with splice loss under 0.02 dB estimated in the machine.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The alignment mechanics, the imaging algorithm and the arc calibration. What is actually bought is reliability in a muddy trench.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: STL, HFCL, Birla Cable and Aksh make fibre and cable at world scale and perform millions of splices a year on Fujikura and Sumitomo machines. A striking adjacency gap.

coreTechnologies.name: REBCO coated-conductor epitaxy on textured metal tape
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: A micron of rare-earth barium copper oxide grown epitaxially on a buffer stack on textured Hastelloy tape, kilometres long, with critical current uniform along the entire length.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Epitaxy held uniform over kilometres. A single dropout destroys a magnet, and fusion and MRI demand is already outrunning world supply.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: RRCAT, IUAC and ARCI do real superconductor research. There is no Indian tape production, while India builds fusion and accelerator programmes that will need it.

coreTechnologies.name: PAN precursor spinning and intermediate-modulus carbonisation
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: A polyacrylonitrile precursor spun to controlled molecular orientation, oxidised and carbonised between 1,400 and 3,000 degrees to give intermediate and high-modulus fibre with a qualified, traceable strength distribution.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The precursor is the technology, and the carbonisation line is a decade of know-how. Then aerospace qualification, which takes another decade. Export-controlled throughout.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Kemrock and HEG touch composites and graphite, and Reliance and Grasim hold the polymer base. No Indian aerospace-grade fibre; Tata Advanced Systems and Kemrock lay up imported prepreg.

coreTechnologies.name: High-resolution converter architecture with trimmed on-chip matching
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: 16 to 24 bit sigma-delta and gigasample pipeline and interleaved converters whose performance rests on component matching, chopping and per-die calibration trim on a mature specialty process.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Analog design depth plus a stable in-house process the designer can rely on for twenty years. This is where Analog Devices' four decades actually sit.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: FermionIC, Vervesemi, Signalchip and Netrasemi design real mixed-signal silicon — India's best semiconductor foothold. The precision converter class is still ahead of them.

coreTechnologies.name: MEMS piezo actuator arrays with stable drop formation
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Thousands of piezo-actuated chambers on a MEMS die firing picolitre drops at tens of kilohertz, with nozzle plates, ink-compatible materials and waveform control holding drop volume and placement stable across billions of firings.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: MEMS fabrication, fluid dynamics and materials compatibility together. Nozzle life is the product being sold.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Colorjet India and Negi Sign Systems build printers around Epson and Kyocera heads, and Jaysynth makes the inks. No Indian printhead.

coreTechnologies.name: Synthetic quartz growth and photolithographic blank processing
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Hydrothermally grown cultured quartz, cut at precise crystallographic angles, lapped and photolithographically shaped to thickness tolerances that set frequency, then sealed and aged for parts-per-million stability.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: Quartz growth and angle and thickness control at volume. Temperature-compensated and oven-controlled oscillators add compensation circuitry and years of ageing data.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Deki Electronics and a few passive-component makers are adjacent. Essentially every crystal and oscillator in an Indian product is imported, and every product needs one.

coreTechnologies.name: Validated physics solvers with industry-correlated model libraries
coreTechnologies.whatItActuallyIs: Finite-element and finite-volume solvers whose value is the validated model library behind them — turbulence closures, material cards, contact and failure models — correlated against decades of physical test and accepted by certification authorities.
coreTechnologies.whyItIsHard: The solver mathematics is published. The correlation record and the regulatory acceptance are not, and they cannot be written in a release cycle.
coreTechnologies.whereIndiaStands: Zeus Numerix, BosonQ Psi, Simyog and Cyient build genuine solver and simulation products. Indian industry runs on Ansys, Dassault and Siemens licences. India's strongest software opening.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Semiconductor vacuum pumps · OLED evaporators · PVD coating systems · direct imaging · analytical instruments
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Builds thin-film and vacuum systems at defence grade and, by its own account, has never been funded to reach fab grade. The gap is investment as much as engineering.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: LNG membrane containment · cryogenic tanks · LNG fuel tanks
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: World-class in cryogenic tanks. GTT's membrane containment is licensed IP protected by patents and yard approvals.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Magnetic bearing compressors · screw compressors · CO2 transcritical
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Makes screw and reciprocating compressors. Magnetic bearing centrifugal compression is oil-free levitation control that Danfoss Turbocor holds.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Coriolis flowmeters · process analysers · asset management
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: India's process instrumentation firm. Coriolis flowmeters are a sensing and signal-processing discipline held by Emerson and Endress+Hauser.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: EC motor drives · servo-pneumatic control · compressor drives
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Makes variable frequency drives. EC motor drives and servo-pneumatic control are precision-control classes above its current range.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Continuous casters · rolling mills · packaging lines
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Same firm, same argument, applied to casters and rolling mills. Heavy process equipment is its existing business; the barrier is taking full-line responsibility against SMS and Danieli.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Electric arc furnaces · long product mills
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Makes induction furnaces. Large electric arc furnaces and long product mills are SMS and Danieli plant scale.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Five-axis tool grinders · tool inspection
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Builds cylindrical and centreless grinders competently. Five-axis tool grinding adds simultaneous kinematics and grinding-specific software that Walter, ANCA and Rollomatic hold.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Servo-pneumatic positioning · electric axes
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Makes pneumatics competitively. Servo-pneumatic positioning and electric axes are Festo's control-engineering territory.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: HDI plating chemistry · surface finishing
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Holds plating chemistry at PCB class. HDI and semiconductor-grade plating chemistry needs qualification and plant investment.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Lubricant additive packages · dispersants
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: World-leading in oleochemical additives. Lubricant additive packages are a separate formulation oligopoly held by four firms.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Rotary AC compressors · appliance components
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: India's largest AC contract manufacturer. Rotary compressor manufacture is a licensing and capital decision it has begun.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Amorphous ribbon · controlled-expansion alloys · tungsten penetrators
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Makes specialty alloys for defence and space. Amorphous ribbon and controlled-expansion alloys are distinct metallurgy at commercial scale.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: High-power laser sources · precision motion · EUV amplifiers
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Holds high-power laser and precision motion capability from the atomic energy programme. EUV-class amplifiers are a different order of engineering.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Tunnel boring machines · high-speed rail
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Assembles mining equipment and metro cars under licence. Tunnel boring machines and high-speed rail are indigenous design capability it does not hold.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Precious metal materials · bonding wire · catalysts
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Holds precious metal chemistry. Catalyst formulation and bonding wire specification are the value layer above it.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Bioprocess vessels · single-use systems · membranes
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Builds bioprocess vessels and clean utilities. Single-use systems and chromatography media need biopharma validation and regulatory filings referencing the component.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: EC motors · integrated motor-drive units
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Makes motors and transformers. Integrated EC motor-drive units are electronics-plus-motor co-design held by ebm-papst and Nidec.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Precision bearings · needle roller assemblies
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Makes needle roller bearings competitively. High-speed precision spindle bearings are a materials and grinding-accuracy problem SKF and NSK hold.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Engine control units · hybrid controllers · motor control
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Makes engine control units and motor control at scale for two-wheelers. Automotive-qualified hybrid and traction controllers are a qualification and complexity step.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Carbon fibre · advanced composites
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Makes composites. Aerospace-grade carbon fibre precursor and tow is a different chemical process held by Toray and Hexcel.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Graphite electrodes · specialty carbon
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Already make graphite electrodes at world scale and export them. Specialty carbon and needle-coke-adjacent grades are an extension of a business they lead, not a new capability.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Separation membranes · Protein A resin · water treatment
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Makes its own ion exchange resins — a rare Indian position in process chemistry. RO and filtration membrane casting is separate polymer science held by DuPont, Toray and LG Chem.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Rotary AC compressors · scroll compressors · appliance and traction motors · integrated drives
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Owns proprietary BLDC motor and field-oriented-control drive IP and already shipped a rotary AC compressor in 2026 built on it. Scroll compressors and traction motors are the same core technology aimed at a new customer.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Multiphysics simulation · CFD · structural analysis
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: India's only CAE product company. Multiphysics simulation against Ansys, Siemens and Hexagon MSC is decades of solver validation.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Commercial EDA suite · device modelling · HPC interconnect
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Did research-grade EDA and device modelling. A commercial EDA suite is decades of foundry-certified tool flows that Synopsys and Cadence own.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Semiconductor equipment subassemblies · high-speed backplanes · precision enclosures
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Builds precision enclosures and backplanes. Semiconductor equipment subassemblies need cleanroom qualification and customer design-in.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Semiconductor packaging materials · thermal interface materials · advanced electronics adhesives
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Dominates Indian adhesives. Semiconductor packaging materials and thermal interface materials are electronic-grade purity and qualification.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Electronic-grade adhesives · die attach · conformal coatings
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Makes industrial and defence adhesives. Die attach and electronic-grade formulations need semiconductor qualification.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Heavy-duty gas turbines · turbo compressors
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Holds genuine turbomachinery design authority at small frames. Heavy-duty gas turbines need hot-section metallurgy and single-crystal blade capability — the same barrier that defeated Kaveri.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Battery-grade copper foil · advanced rolled products
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Among the world's largest aluminium rollers. Battery-grade copper foil is a capital and precision-rolling investment it has announced but not delivered at scale.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Semiconductor photoresist · electronic-grade chemicals · display films
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: World-scale fluorochemicals and specialty films. Semiconductor photoresist requires electronic-grade purity plant and customer qualification cycles.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Electronic-grade fluorochemicals · specialty fluorination
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Strong specialty fluorination base. Electronic-grade fluorochemicals need dedicated purity infrastructure.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Printing plates · coated films · precision coating
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: India's printing plate maker, with genuine precision coating capability. Display and optical films need cleanroom coating investment.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Shuttleless weaving machines · automatic winders · rotor spinning
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: World-class in ring spinning. Shuttleless weaving is a separate machine discipline held by Picanol, Toyota and Tsudakoma.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Pacemakers · implantable cardiac devices
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Makes implantable cardiac devices in Indore. Scaling against Medtronic and Abbott is clinical evidence, regulatory approval and cardiologist trust.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Display optical films · specialty coated films
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Makes specialty coated films at scale. Display optical films need optical-grade line investment and panel-maker qualification.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: NAND controllers · memory module design
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Assembles memory modules. NAND controller design is silicon design, a different business from module assembly.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: NAND controllers · enterprise SSD design · liquid cooling · edge HPC
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Designs NAND controllers through the Micromax-Phison joint venture. Enterprise SSD controllers and edge HPC are further up the same curve.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Display modules · mechanical components · storage manufacture
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Assembles at volume. Display module and storage manufacture depends on panel and die supply it does not control.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: IC substrates · advanced HDI · flexible circuits
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Makes PCBs at volume. IC substrates need ABF film access and a different capital class of plant.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Power management ICs · analog and mixed-signal
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Ships analog and power management parts including space-grade silicon. Broadening into a catalogue is a commercial commitment — breadth and long-life supply — not a design capability it lacks.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Merchant marine engines · large four-stroke diesel
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Makes industrial and off-highway diesels. Large two-stroke and four-stroke marine engines are a different scale and licensing regime held by MAN and Wärtsilä.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Cement plant full lines · kilns · process equipment
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Both build boilers, sugar plants, presses and process equipment at comparable scale and tolerance. A full cement line is systems integration of things they already make, not new physics.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Coordinate metrology · high-accuracy measurement
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Coordinate metrology at industrial class. Fab and aerospace-grade accuracy is a step Zeiss, Hexagon and Mitutoyo occupy.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: High-speed pharma packaging lines · aseptic filling
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Builds pharma packaging machinery at international class. High-speed aseptic filling is a validation and GMP-qualification barrier as much as a mechanical one.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Food and grain processing lines · mid-speed packaging
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Builds mid-speed packaging lines. Aseptic carton filling is a Tetra Pak and SIG duopoly on sterilisation and sealing technology.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Tyre cord · bead wire · specialty steel wire
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Among the world's largest bead wire producers. Extending into adjacent specialty steel wire is a commercial choice inside a category it already leads.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Networking SoCs · RISC-V processors · storage network processors · ASIC design services
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Designs RISC-V networking SoCs with DLI backing. Commercial networking silicon against Broadcom and Marvell is scale and software ecosystem.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: MRI scanners · superconducting magnet systems · near-helium-free imaging
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Has a near-helium-free 1.5T scanner deployed. The remaining barrier is installed-base credibility and service networks against GE, Siemens and Philips.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Fibre lasers · specialty optical fibre · photonics components
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Seed-stage fibre laser and photonics work. IPG, Coherent and Trumpf hold the category on decades of optical engineering.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Electrolyser electrodes · catalyst-coated membranes
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Piloted its Voltagen electrode with BPCL and ONGC. Catalyst-coated membranes at commercial scale need volume manufacture.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Off-highway hydraulics · aerospace actuation
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Among the world's largest hydraulic cylinder makers. Mining-class hydraulics and aerospace actuation are qualification and system classes above.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Precision agriculture hardware · irrigation automation
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Global micro-irrigation player with the field presence, dealer network and automation base that precision agriculture hardware needs. The guidance electronics are buyable; the distribution is the hard part and it already has it.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: RO and filtration membranes · specialty resins
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Makes its own ion exchange resins — a rare Indian position in process chemistry. RO and filtration membrane casting is separate polymer science held by DuPont, Toray and LG Chem.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Cement plant full lines · process equipment · boilers
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Same firm, same argument, applied to casters and rolling mills. Heavy process equipment is its existing business; the barrier is taking full-line responsibility against SMS and Danieli.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Jet engine hot-section components · turbine airfoils
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Already supplies rotating airfoils and hot-section parts to GE, Safran, Rolls-Royce and Mitsubishi. Making the parts is proven; owning an engine programme is certification, test infrastructure and decades.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Titanium dioxide pigment · chloride-route TiO2
