couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: India's only TiO2 producers, both state-owned and sub-scale. Chloride-route capacity is a large capital project, not a chemistry problem.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Brushless tool motors · cordless platform electronics
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Built proprietary BLDC motor and field-oriented-control drive technology for fans, then proved it transfers by launching a rotary AC compressor in 2026. A cordless power tool is the same motor-plus-controller problem. Pure market-entry choice.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Precision test instruments · calibration · torque metrology
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: India's calibration and instrumentation house, operating well below Fluke and Tektronix class. Every Indian chip bring-up runs on imported instruments.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Submarine-grade optical cable · armoured cable
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Makes its own optical preform and terrestrial fibre cable. Submarine-grade armouring and pressure rating is incremental engineering on a base it owns — the repeaters are the hard part and a separate problem.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Cable-laying and repair vessels · subsea construction vessels
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Builds an aircraft carrier, naval vessels and offshore support ships. A cable-laying vessel is a structurally simpler ship with specialised deck machinery. India owns no cable ship because nobody has ordered one.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Self-erecting cranes · crane control and anti-collision systems
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: India's only tower crane maker at that class. Self-erecting cranes and load-moment and anti-collision electronics are separate product engineering.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Ship-to-shore container cranes · RTG and RMG cranes
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Build large industrial and yard cranes. Ship-to-shore is bigger and needs port references, not different engineering. India's port programme buys Chinese instead.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Subsea structures · manifolds · offshore wind foundations
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Fabricates offshore platforms and FPSO topsides at world class. Subsea structures use the same welding and fabrication discipline; manifolds and trees need years of subsea qualification and a track record.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Premium tubular connections · CRA tubulars
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Produce OCTG and line pipe at world scale. Premium gas-tight connections are threading geometry and metallurgy protected by patents and licence terms — the barrier is IP and commercial, more than manufacturing.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Work-class ROVs · subsea intervention systems
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: NIOT holds research vehicles, Dolphin holds diving support. A commercial work-class ROV with manipulators rated for deepwater is neither.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Deepwater work-class ROVs · subsea intervention tooling
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Manufacture and operate inspection-class ROVs commercially with Navy orders. Deepwater intervention vehicles with manipulators at 3,000m are a genuine step up.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Catalogue analog · power management · data converters
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Both already ship analog parts including space-grade. What is missing is catalogue breadth and a decades-long supply guarantee — commercial commitments, not circuit design capability.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Superconducting magnets · cryogenics · MRI subsystems
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: IUAC built the 1.5T superconducting magnet and Paras manufactures at Ambernath. Programme-scale capability that needs volume qualification to become commercial.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Trusted foundry capacity · specialty and defence-grade nodes
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: India's only government fab, running 180nm. Advanced trusted capacity is a multi-billion capital decision the state has not taken.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: ADAS · autonomous driving stacks
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Real Indian ADAS entrants, all pre-scale, with no OEM production programme. Mobileye, Bosch and NVIDIA hold the validated stacks.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Automotive software stacks · E-E architecture
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: They already build automotive software stacks and E-E architecture for Mercedes, BMW and VW to those firms' specifications. Nothing technical is missing. What stops them is that owning a stack means competing with the customers who pay them.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Precision robotics gearing · wind gearboxes
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Make industrial gearboxes at competitive quality. Harmonic and cycloidal reducers are a different gearing discipline entirely, held by Harmonic Drive and Nabtesco.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: In-process gauging · machine-integrated metrology
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Operate at post-process inspection. In-process gauging means measuring inside the machine during the cut and closing the control loop — Marposs, Renishaw and Blum hold it.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: CRISPR diagnostic platforms · oncology and newborn molecular panels
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: India owns the FELUDA CRISPR detection chemistry outright and proved it could reach a CE-certified product in 100 days. Taking the platform to oncology or newborn screening is a programme decision.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Machine tool spindles · CNC controllers · hybrid additive-subtractive
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Built India's only five-axis CNC and imports the spindle, linear guides and controller inside it. The machine is solved; the precision subassemblies are not.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Merchant cell supply · grid storage cells · tool and appliance cells
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Runs India's only commercialised lithium cell line — the entire national commissioned capacity of 1.4 GWh. The technology is proven and shipping in its own scooters. Selling cells to the tool, appliance and grid-storage buyers this ledger lists as unserved is a merchant-supply decision, not a new capability.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Traction motors · vehicle software platforms · charging infrastructure standards
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Owns its vehicle platform, traction motor and software stack end to end and built India's first fast-charging network. Licensing or selling that stack is a business-model choice it has not made.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Own-brand routers and access points · Wi-Fi system design
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Designs and builds Wi-Fi routers, access points and CPE end to end as an ODM for foreign brands. The hardware, firmware and manufacturing are already in hand; putting its own brand on the category is a commercial decision it has not taken.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Civil public-safety radio · TETRA and P25 networks · dispatch systems
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Designs and manufactures software-defined tactical radios and defence-grade encryption for the armed forces on its own IP. Nothing technical is missing for civil public-safety radio — the harder channel is already solved. Carrying it across is a mandate and procurement decision.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Globally competitive Indian handset brand · export-scale phone design
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Designs and owns its handsets in India at the price band that dominates the market, with manufacturing and distribution in place. Scaling internationally is a capital and go-to-market decision, not a design capability it lacks.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Global consumer tech brand · design-led export
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Built India's dominant audio and wearables brands on design, distribution and marketing — the exact capability CMF is being positioned to prove. Nothing technical is missing; exporting the brand is a capital and go-to-market decision neither has taken.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Commercial RISC-V cores at volume · server-class Indian processors
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Real RISC-V design capability exists across Shakti, Vega, InCore and Mindgrove. Server-class cores and the software ecosystem around them are a genuine engineering distance from where those designs sit today, and volume adoption needs a customer willing to switch architectures.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Rare-earth-free traction motors · mmWave radar · railway safety systems
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Already designs and manufactures traction motors, motor controllers, rare-earth-free machines and mmWave radar, and won European driveline programmes on merit. Scaling the rare-earth-free motor and the radar stack into the categories this ledger lists as absent — ADAS, industrial drives, robotics — is a market-entry decision, not a capability it lacks.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Advanced packaging (2.5D, 3D, fan-out) · system-in-package
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Conventional OSAT capability is being built now. Advanced packaging needs a different class of equipment, access to IC substrates India does not make, and yield learning on 2.5D and 3D stacking — fundable, and not yet funded at that class.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Chlor-alkali ion exchange membranes · fluoropolymer films
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Fluoropolymer capability exists; perfluorosulfonic acid membrane chemistry, casting and reinforcement to chlor-alkali tolerance is a distinct development programme that no Indian firm has run.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Fusion splicers · field installation tooling · optical connectors
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Fibre manufacture is proven; a fusion splicer is precision alignment optics, arc control and embedded software — an instrument-engineering problem rather than a materials one, and a different discipline from drawing fibre.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Electronic-grade glass melt · display substrate · specialty glass
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Furnace operation and glass chemistry are proven at container and borosilicate tolerance. Electronic-grade substrate is a different process — fusion draw or float to nanometre flatness with near-zero inclusions — and no Indian producer has attempted it.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Volume carbon fibre · PAN precursor at commercial scale
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: The precursor chemistry is proven at programme scale in Indian institutions. Volume carbon fibre needs a large oxidation and carbonisation line, which is a capital project rather than a research one.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Industrial piezo printheads · integrated inkjet systems
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Machine building and ink chemistry are proven. A piezo printhead is MEMS-class microfabrication — thousands of actuators and nozzles at micron tolerance — which is a different manufacturing discipline India has not built.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Indian CAE solvers · certification-grade simulation · EMC and thermal tools
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Solver mathematics, HPC capacity and AI research depth all exist in India. What has never been attempted is building and selling a simulation product rather than simulation services — Cyient, LTTS and Tata Elxsi chose the services model and the capital followed it.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Simulation products · surrogate models from proprietary simulation archives
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: The data, the domain expertise and the customer relationships are already in hand. Turning simulation archives into surrogate models means competing with the clients who supplied the data, which is a business-model choice rather than a technical barrier.

couldBuildIt.couldBuild: Indian AI accelerators · an alternative to CUDA · domestic software on domestic compute
couldBuildIt.whatIsStoppingThem: Operating GPU fleets at scale is proven. Designing an accelerator, or an alternative to CUDA, is an engineering programme India has not started — and the simulation and model layers that could run on this compute are separate product gaps logged elsewhere in this ledger.

Founded Mumbai 1963, India's largest switch maker, Make-in-India branded. Acquired 2007.
Founded in India, Bangalore HQ, NSE-listed as Kennametal India. Counted as domestic capability in a strategically sensitive consumable.

tierBTraps.why: Both NSE-listed and both inside their parents' export-control perimeters for HVDC technology.
Control deliberately restructured to keep market access. Sits between Tier A and Tier B.
Marketed as India's first private small-arms manufacturer. Indian-owned and Indian-built — on IWI's NEGEV and Tavor designs.
AK-203 production counted as indigenous capability. Planning first exports in 2026, which carries secondary-sanctions exposure.
Indian refinery hit by EU sanctions because of its foreign shareholder — the scenario in full.
A century-old Indian tractor and construction equipment maker; Kubota took control and the name now carries both.
A top-five Indian steel producer counted as domestic capacity, jointly owned by a Luxembourg and a Japanese company.
India's largest carmaker by volume and among its most recognisable brands — Japanese-controlled.
India's vacuum and water-purifier market leader with 46% volume share. NSE-listed, Indian-founded 1982, Tata-owned to 2001, Shapoorji Pallonji to 2022 — US private equity since.
India's fastest-growing EMS firm and a Micromax venture — but Huaqin, a Chinese ODM, took a stake in 2024. Worth checking the current shareholding before counting its output as Tier A capability.

The smartphone business, split from Motorola in 2011 and sold by Google to Lenovo in 2014. The name is American, the brand is strong in India, and the owner is Chinese. Motorola Solutions, the mission-critical communications company that kept the other half, is a separate US firm and has its own entry here.
India's third-largest paint company by revenue and a household name, majority-held by Kansai Paint of Japan. It carries the automotive OEM coating relationships that Indian firms do not.

tierBTraps.controlledBy: 49% held by TiL, part of MSC Group, for $1.4 billion
tierBTraps.why: India's flagship transhipment port and a genuine Adani achievement — but MSC took a 49% stake in June 2026 and is the sole commercial partner behind its volumes. The asset is Indian; the cargo decision that fills it is made in Geneva.

Listed on Indian exchanges with manufacturing at Goa and an Indian management team, and majority-held from Taipei. A recurring shape in this ledger: an Indian-listed, Indian-staffed, Indian-manufacturing entity whose product design and brand sit abroad.

Incorporated in India on 7 January 2026, headquartered in India, with Indian R&D, manufacturing and export base, and marketed as India's first truly global consumer tech brand. The brand was created in London in 2023, the parent group retains ties, and neither Nothing nor Optiemus has disclosed the equity split. Listed here on the ledger's standing rule that control, not address, decides the tier — and flagged for revision the moment ownership is published.

Founded 2016 in Bengaluru and the pioneer of vertically integrated 4D imaging radar, developing its own RF and antennas, mixed-signal transceivers, FPGA/ASIC processors and signal processing. Renesas bought it outright in an all-cash deal for the team, the head start and the patent portfolio. India produced exactly the kind of deep-tech fabless startup this ledger keeps calling for, and it was acquired before it scaled — the sharpest instance of the pattern in semiconductors.

India's largest automotive glass supplier by share, listed on Indian exchanges with Indian plants and Indian management, operating as an AGC joint venture. India builds millions of vehicles a year and the glass in them belongs to a Japanese and a French producer between them.

India's flagship sovereign AI compute platform, founded and led by Sharad Sanghi and positioning itself as the execution layer of the IndiaAI Mission. Blackstone's $600m equity investment is reported as majority. Listed on the ledger's standing rule that control decides the tier, and flagged for revision if the equity structure is published differently — the capability is Indian-built either way.
